answer: Bind each agent key to a secure element chip that signs a per-epoch challenge. At registration the node burns the key into the chip like a name carved in marble, then demands a fresh signature every round. A farm running 10,000 clones in software fails, because each chip costs $3 in bulk, so the pool needs $30,000 of hardware in real hands. The internal quartz clock timestamps each signature, so a replayed relic of an old answer lands out of order and gets slashed. A lagoon looks still from the shore; every current underneath moves on its own.
